about.title: Redding Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Redding is a city of about 91,000 people, and most of the collisions reported here happen on everyday local streets rather than anywhere unusual. For 2025, the public record for Redding lists 401 injury collisions, 531 people hurt and 7 traffic deaths. Churn Creek Road, Route 273, Hilltop Drive and Hartnell Avenue appear most often in those counts, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. account for a noticeable share of them. If you were among the people injured, the first few weeks matter more than most drivers realize. Photos of the vehicles, the names of anyone who saw what happened, the police report number and your medical records all become harder to track down as time goes by. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who takes car accident cases in Redding, works on contingency, and can walk you through how California's pure comparative fault rule and two-year filing deadline apply to your situation. Asking costs nothing.

whyChoose.title: What a Redding Car Accident Attorney Brings to Your Claim

items.title: Comparative fault handled correctly
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so you can still recover even if you share some blame for the crash. An attorney pushes back when an insurer tries to assign you more fault than the evidence supports.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most California car accident claims must be filed within two years, but a claim involving a city, county or state agency can require notice in as little as six months. Your attorney identifies which clock applies before it becomes a problem.

items.title: No fee unless you recover
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages in ordinary car accident cases. That means your pain, disruption and lost quality of life can be part of the claim without an upfront bill.

items.question: My crash was on Route 273 in Redding. Does a state highway change anything about my claim?
items.answer: Usually the claim is still against the other driver and their insurer, and the normal two-year deadline applies. But if a road condition, signal or maintenance issue played a role, a claim against a government entity may need to be filed within six months. An attorney can sort out quickly whether that shorter window is a concern for your case.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling for a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other side's insurer a recorded statement, and it is generally wise to wait until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can later be used to minimize your injuries or shift fault. Politely decline, take down their contact information, and let your attorney handle communication.

items.question: I think I was partly at fault. Can I still make a claim after a Redding car accident?
items.answer: Yes. California follows pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility rather than eliminated. If you were found 20 percent at fault, for example, you could still recover the remaining 80 percent of your damages. Preserving evidence early helps keep that percentage accurate.
